question: Let \(S\) be the set of all positive integer divisors of \(100{,}000.\) How many numbers are the product of two distinct elements of \(S?\)
solution:
The useful way to distinguish products is by their prime exponents. Since
\[
100{,}000=2^5\cdot5^5,
\]
every element of \(S\) has the form \(2^i5^j\), where \(0\le i,j\le5\). Thus every product of two elements has the form \(2^a5^b\), where \(0\le a,b\le10\). There are \(11\cdot11=121\) candidate exponent pairs.

Four pairs are impossible when the factors must be distinct:
\[
(0,0),\quad(0,10),\quad(10,0),\quad(10,10).
\]
Indeed, an exponent sum of \(0\) forces both corresponding factor exponents to be \(0\), while a sum of \(10\) forces both to be \(5\). At each of these four pairs, the two factors are therefore forced to be equal.

To show that every other pair works, construct factors as follows:

| Exponent ranges | Two factors in \(S\) | Factors equal only at |
|---|---|---|
| \(0\le a\le5,\ 0\le b\le5\) | \(1\) and \(2^a5^b\) | \((0,0)\) |
| \(6\le a\le10,\ 0\le b\le5\) | \(2^5\) and \(2^{a-5}5^b\) | \((10,0)\) |
| \(0\le a\le5,\ 6\le b\le10\) | \(5^5\) and \(2^a5^{b-5}\) | \((0,10)\) |
| \(6\le a\le10,\ 6\le b\le10\) | \(2^55^5\) and \(2^{a-5}5^{b-5}\) | \((10,10)\) |

These four ranges cover every candidate pair exactly once. Every displayed factor has prime exponents between \(0\) and \(5\), and each displayed product is \(2^a5^b\). Except at the four excluded pairs, the factors are distinct. Unique prime factorization also ensures that different pairs \((a,b)\) give different numbers.

Therefore the number of possible products is
\[
121-4=\boxed{117},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
